reason: E1 and E2 support that lattice distortion from atomic size mismatch enhances solid-solution strengthening and reduces thermal softening in BCC HEAs, but they do not involve Mo or TiVNbTa. E3 shows that NbTaTiV exhibits edge-dislocation-dominated deformation with low strain-rate sensitivity, but it does not link Mo addition to a shift in dislocation mechanism or demonstrate this at 1273 K. No cited evidence addresses Mo solubility, phase stability, or ductility in TiVNbTa, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Mo addition increases solid-solution strengthening via lattice distortion in BCC HEAs
Lattice distortion reduces thermal softening and improves high-temperature strength retention
Edge dislocation dominance at high temperature yields better strength retention than screw dislocation dominance
Mo addition can shift dislocation mechanism from screw- to edge-dominated at high temperature
5–10 at% Mo maintains single-phase BCC structure and sufficient ductility in TiVNbTa
